thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT: production: inference-router pool 'runtime-pool-3' experiencing KV cache growth and continuous-batching timeouts. p95 latency spike -> 4.2s, rate of 5xx increased from 0.4% to 6.7%. Detected memory pressure on several GPU nodes. Paging on-call.
alex.nguyen: on it. linking dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/inference-router?from=-30m
alex.nguyen: initial quick check — tailing runtime logs shows repeated KV cache shard evictions then immediate repopulate loops.
maya.patel: I think this matches the MQA/KV blowup pattern we saw in nov patch where tokenization changes produced many unique KV keys. Which models are hot?
infra-bot: Top callers by model (last 10m): mistral-8x7b-v2: 31%, qwen-mqa-6b: 27%, llm-7b-qa: 12%.
alex.nguyen: qwen-mqa-6b is suspicious. Those sessions show extremely long contexts and repeated re-tokenization; KV entries growing unbounded.
jamie: can someone run a conservative mitigation: disable continuous batching on runtime-pool-3 and force KV shard gc? I'll prepare a k8s patch.
maya.patel: +1. Also add a temporary prefix-hash cap tweak so we don't create new shards per session.

jamie: pushing quick hotfix now — patch below:
```
# reduce continuous batching window and disable prefix caching
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-batching-config
data:
  continuous_batch_enabled: "false"
  max_batch_size: "8"
  kv_prefix_shard_cap: "10000"
```
kubectl -n inference apply -f runtime-batching-config.yaml
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-router-pool-3
```

alex.nguyen: applied. rolling restart starting. watching pods.
infra-bot: rollout status: 3/3 updated. latency trending down to 1.1s p95 after restart.
maya.patel: good. also triggered KV eviction across pool-3:
```
# force eviction script
for pod in $(kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-router -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n inference exec $pod -- /usr/local/bin/kvctl --evict-stale --shards=all
done
```

jamie: eviction completed.
alex.nguyen: error rate dropped from 6.7% -> 0.9% within 6m. p95 back near baseline but p99 still elevated.
maya.patel: p99 elevated due to long-context Qwen sessions — since continuous batching is off, they don't get harmful batching but some sessions still rebuild huge KV entries. We're throttling long-session requests at the router now (soft reject > 120k tokens/session).
priya: heads-up: support -> notified 3 customers (acct-A, acct-B, acct-C) seeing partial failures for long-context Q&A endpoints. CS has an incident banner ready.
samir: taking over this incident (oncall handoff). Summary: KV cache growth caused by Qwen-MQA long-context sessions + tokenization mismatches creating many unique KV prefixes. Hotfix applied: continuous batching disabled on pool-3, kv_prefix_shard_cap lowered, forced KV eviction, soft throttling for >120k tokens. Impact: transient 5xx for some long-context customers, broader latency spike. Current status: degraded -> recovering.
alex.nguyen: added a rollback plan if this hotfix causes throughput regressions: re-enable continuous batching with max_batch_size=16 and add per-model batch policy for qwen-mqa to use strict prefix dedup.
samir: next steps:
- monitor p99 and OOMs for 2h (maya)
- run a replay test against qwen-mqa with representative sessions to reproduce locally (jamie)
- create a model-specific adapter for MQA tokenization alignment (eng-ml)
- notify enterprise customers with risk of long-context failures (priya)

maya.patel: quick note — logs show repeated "KV: new prefix key mismatch" entries originating from tokenization step when model variant is qwen-mqa-8k vs qwen-mqa-32k. Looks like MQA/packetization changes created inconsistent prefixing across variants.
jamie: can confirm a small repro: feed same user stream through qwen-mqa-8k and qwen-mqa-32k -> different prefix hash, both stored, then merged later causing duplication and growth. I'll file a reducer PR to normalize prefix hashing across MQA variants.

infra-bot: metric alert cleared for p95 >3s. p99 still above threshold; follow-up alert set for 30m.
samir: handover notes for next shift @oncall: keep continuous batching disabled until model adapter landed and we validate prefix normalization. If we re-enable batching, do staged ramp on canary nodes only.
alex.nguyen: added incident tag and created postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.internal/incidents/kv-cache-qwen-mqa-1743006789
priya: support message posted to affected accounts. sales notified.
maya.patel: root cause hypothesis: MQA tokenization variant mismatch + continuous-batching optimization that assumed stable prefix hashing -> cache explosion when variant mismatch created many ephemeral prefixes. We'll prioritize a fix in adapter that canonicalizes prefixes before cache keying.
samir: closing loop for now — monitoring. ping me for escalations. :thumbsup:
